text:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT - reserved-pool resv-pool-7 GPU utilization 100% + queue growth detected. autoscaler reported ERROR: quota_exceeded when attempting scale-up at 18:01 UTC. Affects Dedicated tenants on us-west2.

maria (oncall): I'm on it. first pass: which tenants hit throttles? any customer 5xx reports?

devon (infra): metric dump: queue_length: 1220, avg_latency_tokens: 340ms, p95_latency: 1.8s. recent autoscale attempts: 3 -> all failed with `QuotaError: insufficient vgpu quota` from cloud provider.

maria (oncall): ack. tagging ry an @ryan for routing/fallback policy changes. ryan please weigh in on model fallbacks.

ryan: on it. quick question — are these all reserved GPUs consumed by noisy tenant(s) or is autoscaler failing to request new nodes?

devon (infra): both. reserved pool shows all 12 GPUs assigned. eviction history shows repeated short sessions from tenant "streamline-ai" hogging NVMe-backed instances; noisy sessions not evicting due to sticky reservations. autoscaler calls to cloud returned 429/QuotaError.

maria (oncall): ok priority: 1) reduce customer-facing impact 2) unblock queue 3) remediate noisy tenant 4) escalate quota with cloud if needed.

amanda (cs): getting a ping from AcmeHealth — multiple timeouts hitting our API. they report degraded inference throughput. I'll open a bridge with them after we have a status for impact.

lee: quick mitigation idea: enable per-tenant soft-throttling to shed best-effort non-enterprise traffic and free up reserved GPUs for enterprise tenants. I can flip that flag in the routing layer in ~2min. need approval.

maria (oncall): do it. prioritize enterprise tenants. post exact command when done.

lee: flipping route policy now. command: 

```
curl -X POST \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ 
  https://routing.internal/api/v1/policies/soft_throttle \ 
  -d '{"scope":"non_enterprise","throttle_pct":80}'
```

lee: response 200. non-enterprise traffic throttled 80%.

ops-bot: ROUTE_CHANGE: policy soft_throttle applied by lee at 18:04 UTC. predicted queue reduction: ~60%.

maria (oncall): seeing queue drop to 520 — good. p95 latency for enterprises back to 900ms. AcmeHealth still reports some 502s but less frequent. amanda pls update customer: we prioritized enterprise traffic and are working on longer-term fix.

amanda (cs): sending update to AcmeHealth now. will ask for any additional logs/IDs.

devon (infra): next: noisy tenant eviction. we should trigger eviction for long-running sessions exceeding 45m in resv-pool-7. using eviction-service API to mark sessions for preemptive reclaim.

maria (oncall): go ahead devon. ensure we target sessions with >75% GPU utilization first. call out to infra team if collateral risk.

devon (infra): running eviction dry-run to list candidates: 

```
curl -s -X GET "https://evictor.internal/v1/pools/resv-pool-7/candidates?min_runtime=2700&min_gpu_util=0.75" | jq '.sessions | length '
```

devon (infra): dry-run returned 18 sessions. initiating soft-evict sequence (notify -> 30s grace -> force-terminate).

ops-bot: EVICT_INITIATED by devon at 18:09 UTC for 18 sessions in resv-pool-7.

ryan: also adding routing fallback: enterprise tenants in this pool will be routed to a quantized variant (gpt-small-q4) where acceptable. updating model mapping now.

ryan: applying model-fallback mapping: 

```
PATCH /api/v1/projects/enterprise-routing
payload: {"fallback_model":"gpt-small-q4","target_tenants":["AcmeHealth","Brightleaf"]}
```

ryan: mapping applied. expected CPU token cost reduction ~2.6x.

maria (oncall): monitoring customer error rates. metrics look better. p95 enterprise latency 650ms. queue under 300.

amanda (cs): AcmeHealth on call, they confirmed fewer errors. still some in-flight failures from older requests. they appreciate the update.

lee: quick note — autoscaler reports still failing due to cloud quota. opened support ticket with provider (case# 555-ACME-Q). submitting scaling workaround request.

devon (infra): as a belt-and-suspenders: I'm going to reassign two short-lived burst GPUs from shared pool to resv-pool-7 to handle remaining spike. manual allocate executed: 

```
internalctl pools move --from shared-burst --to resv-pool-7 --gpus 2 --force
```

devon (infra): allocation succeeded.

ops-bot: MANUAL_ALLOCATION applied by devon at 18:16 UTC. new reserved gpu count: 14.

maria (oncall): excellent. now for the handoff: I'm going to pass this to ryan for post-incident follow-ups (quota escalation, longer-term eviction heuristics, routing policy tuning). ryan — you are the oncall owner for the next hour?

ryan: I can take it. handing my personal oncall baton to maria in 1h for the rotation.

maria (oncall): creating follow-up ticket for root cause + remediation: 
- escalate cloud quota (case# 555-ACME-Q)
- adjust eviction threshold to 30m for high-util tenants in resv pools
- add autoscaler retry jitter and backoff for quota errors
- add alert for reserved-pool-sustained-queue >300 for 5m

maria (oncall): also creating a customer postmortem stub and assigning Amanda to coordinate comms.

amanda (cs): got it. will prepare message templates and SLO impact note.

lee: final note — we'll run a quick experiment to ban noisy tenant's burst sessions if they exceed 3 concurrent sessions on reserved pools. will propose in follow-up.

ops-bot: INCIDENT_UPDATE: reduced impact, queue stabilized. current queue: 48. enterprise p95 latency: 420ms. open action items recorded in INC-2026.

maria (oncall): closing active pager. handing full incident ownership to ryan for follow-up. thanks all for quick triage :thumbsup:

ryan: leaving final ack — pls ping if anything re-escalates. I'll drive the quota case and eviction policy change tomorrow.

pagerbot: Reminder: please add postmortem details to the incident doc and set severity (S2 recommended).

maria (oncall): added severity S2. end of thread.
